Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The two Australian openers, Usman Khawaja and Sam Konstas, make their way out to the middle, followed by the West Indies players. Jayden Seales to start proceedings with the ball. Let's go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Right then, Australia have around 40 minutes to bat before Stumps, light permitting, as Ian Bishop mentioned on air. This could be a challenging little phase for the openers, and they'll be keen to get through it unscathed. West Indies, on the other hand, will be eyeing an early breakthrough to head into ‘Moving Day’ with momentum on their side. Join us in a bit to catch all the action.

Australia would’ve hoped for a bigger first-innings lead, but they’ll still believe they hold the upper hand and can dictate terms going forward. Josh Hazlewood, as so often, struck early to set the tone, and Pat Cummins followed up with a brilliant reflex catch off his own bowling to dismiss Keacy Carty. While the bowlers did apply pressure, there were phases where they allowed a few too many runs to slip through. Cummins ended with two, Hazlewood also claimed a couple, and Nathan Lyon made the most of the conditions to pick up three crucial wickets. Mitchell Starc and Travis Head eventually cleaned up the tail, but not before the West Indies lower order dug in and added some vital runs, frustrating the bowlers and narrowing the gap.

West Indies have shown tremendous grit with the bat and didn’t allow Australia to run away with the game. Although they lost Kraigg Brathwaite early, they recovered well. John Campbell looked solid during his knock of 40, but once again failed to convert his start. The standout performer, though, was Brandon King, who led the charge with a fine 75, forming two vital partnerships, first with Roston Chase and then with Hope. The two Josephs and the tail also chipped in with valuable contributions down the order, adding over 50 together and helping the Windies narrow the deficit to just 33 runs.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Travis Head's part time spin finally comes to Australia's rescue as they bowl out West Indies for 253. This delivery is not short enough to be played off the back foot, the line is on off, Anderson Phillip stays back and punches it off the toe end of the bat, back to the bowler. Travis Head goes low to his right and plucks a good catch. It is sent upstairs for checking. The third umpire feels the fingers are underneath the ball when the catch is taken. OUT appears on the big screen. West Indies have been bowled out for 253!

West Indies, however, managed to weather the storm for a while as King and Shai Hope stitched together a steady 58-run stand, with King bringing up his maiden Test fifty in the process. That partnership helped chip away at the deficit, bringing it down to under 120. But just when things seemed to be settling, skipper Pat Cummins produced a peach to dismiss Hope, sparking another slide. Nathan Lyon then got into the act, grabbing two crucial wickets, including the prized scalp of King. Australia will now be eager to clean up the tail quickly without giving away too many, while the Windies' lower order will aim to inch as close to parity as possible. ... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

The second session on Day 1 was dominated by batters, and that is something that will concern the Aussies. West Indies, on the other hand, have two set batters at the crease, and they will feel optimistic going into the second session with 7 wickets in hand. With the West Indies trailing by 176 runs, the next session could very well be decisive in the context of the game. So, do join us for the post-Lunch session at 4.40 PM GMT.

At 64/3, the Aussies had their noses in front. However, an intentful, unbeaten 46-run stand between King and Chase has shifted the momentum in WI's favor. The former in particular has looked to put away anything poor and is currently unbeaten on 39. Roston Chase has been playing second fiddle and has looked assured in his short stay. For the Aussies, their frontline pace trio and Webster were disciplined as always. Considering the amount of seam, swing, and variable bounce in the offing, the Aussie pacers will feel they have sort of underperformed in that session. Lyon bowled 2 overs at the fag end of the session, and there appeared to be some help for him. So going into the second session, with the old Dukes ball, his role could be crucial.

SESSION SUMMARY - 110 Runs, 28 Overs, 3 Wickets. That will be the end of the first session on Day 2. One feels the West Indies might have piped out this session by a slight margin, as the conditions were challenging, but they have managed to lose just 3 wickets and have scored at a healthy rate close to 4 runs an over. The West Indies innings started with the early wicket of Kraigg Brathwaite, who perished for a duck in his 100th game. After that, Carty, who came in at number 3, didn’t last for long, as a stunner from Cummins of his own bowling got the better of him. Campbell at the other end wasn’t fazed by the proceedings as he batted positively for his 40 from the word go before ending up playing one shot too many as he perished of Webster's bowling.
